sources.entry: Headscale | Self-hosted implementation of the Tailscale control server

summary.one_liner: Headscale is an open source, self-hosted implementation of the Tailscale control server, written for running a single personal or small-organisation tailnet.
summary.what_it_does: The control server is the component that exchanges WireGuard public keys between nodes in a Tailscale network, assigns client IP addresses, sets boundaries between users, enables machine sharing, and exposes advertised routes. Headscale aims to provide this as a self-hosted alternative for hobbyists and small open-source organisations, with a deliberately narrow scope of one tailnet. The README points to separate documentation for stable and development versions covering features and client OS support. It also describes development builds from the main branch as container images and binaries. The README says a NixOS module is available in the nix/ directory. Development uses Go, Buf for Protobuf generation, and linting with golangci-lint, buf, clang-format, mdformat and prettier.
use_cases: run a private WireGuard mesh VPN for a personal lab
manage node keys and IP assignment for a tailnet
share machines and advertised routes between nodes
run an open-source alternative to Tailscale's coordination service
notable: Open source, self-hosted replacement for the Tailscale control server
Narrow scope: a single tailnet aimed at personal use or small organisations
Development builds from main available as container images and binaries
NixOS module provided in nix/ directory
Integration testing used to reimplement Tailscale behaviour, per the linked talks
caveats: The README states the project does not support or encourage running Headscale behind reverse proxies or in containers
The main branch may contain unreleased changes; the README advises using the matching release tag
Not associated with Tailscale Inc.; Tailscale-owned proprietary GUI clients and the official control server remain separate
keywords: ip address assignment for vpn clients
